title: Hull warn against moving play-off final as Middlesbrough call for Southampton’s expulsion
content:
Hull City head coach Sergej Jakirovic is urging the EFL not to rearrange next weekend’s Championship play-off final after seeing his team become “collateral damage” in the Southampton ‘spygate’ saga.

Tuesday’s semi-final second leg saw Southampton provisionally book a place with an extra-time win but opponents Middlesbrough have publicly called for the south-coast side to be hit with a sporting sanction and thrown out of the play-offs. Southampton have been charged with a breach of the EFL rules after it was alleged a member of their backroom team spied on a Middlesbrough training session two days before the sides met in their first leg.

“The conduct at issue, namely the observation and recording of our training session ahead of a fixture of such significance, goes to the heart of sporting integrity and fair competition,” Middlesbrough said on Friday. “In these circumstances, the only appropriate response is a sporting sanction which would prevent Southampton FC from participating in the EFL Championship play-off final.”

Hull, meanwhile, moved to within 90 minutes of the Premier League on Monday night when they sealed a 2-0 aggregate win over Millwall in their two-legged semi-final.

That impressive victory has taken Jakirovic’s side back to Wembley for the first time since the 2016 Championship play-off final but their progress has been overshadowed by the ongoing uncertainty over their opponents.

An independent disciplinary hearing, scheduled for no later than next Tuesday, will decide Southampton’s fate but the EFL raised the prospect of the final, scheduled for a week on Saturday, being delayed. That means that Hull cannot currently be sure who they will face or when they will play a game potentially worth £200million ($266m) to the winners.

“I can say we, Hull City, are collateral damage,” said Jakirovic, speaking to The Athletic at the club’s training ground this afternoon. “Nobody is speaking about us. We deserved to beat Millwall over two games. We proved everything on the pitch, everything is clear.

“To me, the biggest problem is if they postpone the Saturday game. This would be the biggest problem. How can you keep focus and concentration of the players after a very long season?

“When we won at Millwall on Monday, already we start to prepare for (next) Saturday’s game. We started to prepare for Southampton on Tuesday because they won.”

Hull have spent the last two days training with Southampton in mind and will step up their preparations on Monday, following a weekend of rest for the Hull players.

Any tactical plans drawn up could, in theory, be scrapped if Southampton were expelled from the play-offs, with a focus then having to turn quickly to Middlesbrough if they are granted a place in the final.

Jakirovic said he can empathise with Middlesbrough boss Kim Hellberg, who was visibly upset after Tuesday’s defeat, but accepts his focus has to be on Southampton.

“Our complete focus and concentration is on the final,” added Jakirovic. “The investigation is going on so we will see what will happen.

“I can imagine how Kim Hellberg feels. Our full focus is on the final game and this is Southampton. Southampton is our opponent because they beat Middlesbrough in two games so I am expecting Southampton. If they change something, then we will prepare for another game.”

As The Athletic previously reported, Middlesbrough had wanted to participate in the hearing, but confirmed officially on Friday this request had been denied.

“The club regrets that outcome, given we are directly affected by the matters under consideration and hold relevant factual evidence as to the events in question and their competitive impact,” their statement added.

“We remain hopeful that the EFL, as regulator, will pursue such a sanction before the Disciplinary Commission in order to protect the integrity of the game, safeguard all member clubs, and deter any attempt in the future to obtain an unfair and unlawful advantage in pursuit of promotion to the Premier League.”

Ahead of Tuesday night’s second leg, Phil Parsons, Southampton’s chief executive, published a letter on the club’s website that stated they are “fully cooperating with the EFL and the disciplinary commission” but also want to ensure “all the facts and context are properly understood”.
